Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Town, shops & places

local adjective

also locals, local people, home-grown

classical

Varr. LL 5.77: aquātilium vocābula partim sunt vernācula partim peregrīna (Lewis & Short)
Col. 8.2.5: gallīnae (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. local

vernāculus, vernācula, vernāculum

adjective, declension

local, native, home-grown (of produce, breeds and words)

Lewis & Short: “native, domestic, indigenous”, the classical sense, as against peregrīnus, foreign: local hens and vines, local names. Morgan–Owens gives it for “local”, and ferculum vernāculum for a local speciality.

Other words

  • vīcīnus, vīcīna, vīcīnum — nearby, of the neighbourhood

    adjective, declension · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.14.24: nec vīcīna subest vīnum praebēre taberna; Liv. 1.14.6: bellum (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx ut adjectīvum plērumque poētica: Hor., Verg., Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā Liv.)

    The shop or the tavern round the corner. As an adjective mostly poetic (Lewis & Short); in prose vīcīnus is mostly the noun, a neighbour (see neighbour), and the local people are the vīcīnitās (see community).

  • locālis, locāle — of a place, local

    adjective, third declension · also used · late Latin · Tert. Scap. 3; Amm. 14.7.5 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 341: numerus locālis, a local telephone number

    Late Latin; Traupman uses it for a local call. Classical Latin says vernāculus or vīcīnus.

Examples

  • nec vīcīna subest vīnum praebēre taberna quae possit tibi

    and there is no tavern nearby that could serve you wineHor. Ep. 1.14.24–25

  • vernācula: lactūca ā lacte, quod holus id habet lac

    native plants: lettuce, lactūca, from lac, milk, because the plant has milk in itVarr. LL 5.104

See also community, neighbour, local train.

SourcesLewis & Short: vernaculus · Lewis & Short: vicinus · Lewis & Short: localis

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. local.
